newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat falls sharply late on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat falls sharply late on fund selling.

text.p: Aggressive fund selling, tied to long liquidation amid a technical breakdown, drove CBOT wheat futures to a sharply lower close in fast trading, traders said.
"It was fund selling and long liquidation," said Cargill Investor Services wheat analyst, Warren King. "There were, I think, about 10 million bushels worth of stops hit late."
Traders said sell stops were hit in the July at $3.78 per bushel, which was just above the second support level of $3.77-1/2 seen on technicians charts early Thursday.
Fundamentalists cited rainy weather in the Plains.

The U.S. soft red winter wheat crop has received enough moisture to get the crop off to a rapid start out of dormancy and the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region this week found crop-enhancing showers in the south. Plus there are forecasts for more rain in the key Kansas HRW area.

The wheat market had shown signs of a technical breakdown during two consecutive sessions of lower closes and even a "satisfactory" USDA weekly export sales tally could not stem the tide of late fund long liquidation, traders noted.
Wheat closed three to 13-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down 13-1/2 at $3.75. July was down 13 at $3.73.

"They were a little cautious yesterday (about selling) on fears of getting a bullish export sales report today and they didn't get it," King said. "There is nothing in the wheat market to support it right now."
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended March 27 totaled 253,200 tonnes, just above the high end of expectations for 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes.
The four- and 20-day moving averages (MA) for the May contract were giving off bullish signals early Thursday. The four-day MA for May was at $3.95-1/4 and the 20-day was at $3.86.

Technicians said first support in the May was at $3.85 and second support was at $3.77-1/2. The session low for May was $3.72. First resistance was at $3.92-1/2 and second resistance was at $4.00. The session high for May was $3.89.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 36-1/2 percent. The market generally views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
In late dealings, Smith Barney sold two million bushels of July, Iowa Grain sold 2.5 million and LFG Futures sold one million July, traders said.
On the day, Refco Inc sold three million bushels of July, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of July, the traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 22,000 contracts, below the 25,945 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 350 July $3.50 July $3.50 puts at 7-3/4 cents, LFG Futures bought 200 July $3.60 calls at 32 cents and sold 200 July $3.80 calls at 21 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, below the 7,492 traded Wednesday.
